about.title: Hello, I'm
about.name: Esther.
paragraphs: As a digital project manager and delivery partner, I'm the person you call when you have a digital ambition that needs to become real.

Moving quickly to understand your unique challenges comes naturally to me. Leading a strategic whiteboard session with your management team or running a technical review with your developers, both feel equally at home. My core strength is acting as the connective tissue across disciplines - bridging the gap between IT, creative, and business, and making sure complex work actually crosses the finish line.

Straightforward solutions and tangible action win over lengthy reports, every time. When we work together, you will always know where things stand - and you will always get a partner who takes ownership of the work.

work.archiveTitle: More things made clear, useful and real

items.label: 01 / BRAND + WEBSITE
items.title: A personal brand for experiencing Amsterdam with a knowledgeable local friend.
items.character: Warm, worldly and personal - more local companion than tour operator.
items.summary: Dennis needed to feel like a cultured, welcoming host rather than a standard tour operator.
items.needed: The project needed to make Dennis feel knowledgeable, personal and distinctly Amsterdam, without falling into the usual tour-guide language.
items.direction: The identity leans into warmth, editorial detail and Amsterdam-inspired cues so the site feels like meeting a local companion before booking a tour.
items.outcome: The result gives Dennis a sharper digital welcome and a clearer way to show the kind of Amsterdam experience he offers.
items.credits: Role and collaborator credits still need final confirmation before detailed public attribution.

items.label: 02 / BRAND + WEBSITE
items.title: A bold, candid digital home for a photographer who puts people at ease.
items.character: Editorial, playful and direct - just like the person behind the camera.
items.summary: Ingrid needed to feel warm and personal without becoming soft, beige or predictable.
items.needed: The site needed to carry Ingrid’s warmth, humour and directness while still helping visitors quickly understand her services and booking route.
items.direction: Candid portraits, editorial typography and vivid action moments make the site feel personal, useful and unmistakably Ingrid.
items.outcome: The finished direction gives Ingrid a digital home that connects her story, work, practical information and booking path in one place.
items.credits: Role and collaborator credits still need final confirmation before detailed public attribution.

items.label: 03 / UX + APP PROTOTYPE
items.title: Turning a recipe idea into something people could see, understand and try.
items.character: From loose idea to a first experience people could test.
items.summary: The recipe-app idea needed a clear first experience before full development made sense.
items.needed: The idea needed one understandable journey, not a complete future product. The prototype had to make the core experience visible and testable.
items.direction: The work focused on the first useful loop: what someone sees, chooses, follows and learns from in the recipe experience.
items.outcome: The prototype turned discussion into something concrete enough to show, try and improve before a larger investment.
items.credits: Role and collaborator credits still need final confirmation before detailed public attribution.

items.label: 04 / SERVICE DESIGN + LAUNCH
items.title: Making a complex certification process understandable from end to end.
items.character: Complex moving parts made easier to understand and prepare for use.
items.summary: A complex certification journey needed clearer handoffs, testing and launch preparation.
items.needed: The work needed to connect journeys, handoffs and onboarding details so the experience could be understood before it reached users.
items.direction: The focus was clarity over decoration: mapping what users and teams needed to understand at each step.
items.outcome: The work helped prepare a complex platform journey for testing, onboarding and launch.
items.credits: Some details may need to remain redacted. Public case material should only use approved non-confidential artifacts.

studio.title: Small by design. Serious about the work.

items.title: I need a brand
items.situation: You have a good business or idea, but you do not yet know how to explain it or what it should look like.
items.result: We clarify what you offer, what people should remember, and how the business should feel. I turn that into a visual identity you can use consistently.
items.example: Dennis Gerrits needed to feel like a knowledgeable Amsterdam friend, not a conventional tour operator.

items.title: I need a website
items.situation: You need a website, or your current one no longer shows the quality or personality of the business.
items.result: We decide what visitors need to understand, structure the pages, create the visual design and build a responsive website that is ready to use.
items.example: Studio Ingrid de Reuver needed a site that felt warm and personal without looking like a predictable photography template.

items.title: I want to test an idea
items.situation: You have an idea for an app, digital service or new feature, but you do not want full development before you know whether it works.
items.result: We choose the most important user journey, work out how the idea should function and create a clickable prototype people can understand and try.
items.example: For HAP, the recipe-app idea became a concrete flow and clickable first version.

usp.title: First, I look for what needs to come through.
usp.copy: The right visual direction usually starts before the colours and type. I look for the details, tone and point of view that make the business recognizable. That becomes the thread through the identity, the website and every interaction.
steps: Listen for the useful detail, not the loudest claim.
